servT.sk: 12 až 16 porcií (vyjde jeden cheesecake s priemerom 23 cm)

time.en: not given | Cook: not given | Total: not given

en.v: The cheesecake can be refrigerated for up to 4 days.

sk.v: Cheesecake môžete uchovávať v chladničke až 4 dni.

en.t: 113 g graham cracker crumbs (8 whole crackers, broken into rough pieces and processed in food processor until uniformly fine)
1 tbsp (12 g) granulated sugar
6 tbsp (85 g) unsalted butter, melted, divided, 1 tbsp (14 g) is melted for greasing pan
1134 g cream cheese, cut into rough 2.5 cm chunks and left to stand at room temperature for 30 to 45 minutes
1/8 tsp (0.8 g) table salt
298 g granulated sugar
71 g sour cream
2 tsp (10 ml) lemon juice from 1 lemon
2 tsp (10 ml) vanilla extract
2 large egg yolks (≈36 g)
6 large eggs (≈300 g without shell)

1. For the crust: Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and heat oven to 165 °C (fan 145 °C). Combine graham cracker crumbs and sugar in medium bowl; add 5 tbsp (70 g) melted butter and toss with fork until evenly moistened. Brush bottom and sides of 23 cm springform pan with most of remaining melted butter, making sure to leave enough to brush pan in step 4.
2. Empty crumbs into springform pan and press evenly into pan bottom. Bake until fragrant and beginning to brown around edges, about 13 minutes. Cool on wire rack while making filling.

3. For the cheesecake filling: Increase oven temperature to 260 °C (fan 240 °C). In standing mixer fitted with paddle attachment, beat cream cheese at medium-low speed to break up and soften slightly, about 1 minute. Scrape beater and bottom and sides of bowl well with rubber spatula; add salt and about half of sugar and beat at medium-low speed until combined, about 1 minute. Scrape bowl; beat in remaining sugar until combined, about 1 minute. Scrape bowl; add sour cream, lemon juice, and vanilla, and beat at low speed until combined, about 1 minute. Scrape bowl; add yolks and beat at medium-low speed until thoroughly combined, about 1 minute. Scrape bowl; add whole eggs two at a time, beating until thoroughly combined, about 1 minute, and scraping bowl between additions.

4. Brush sides of springform pan with remaining melted butter. Set springform pan on rimmed baking sheet (to catch any spills if springform pan leaks). Pour filling into cooled crust and bake 10 minutes; without opening oven door, reduce oven temperature to 95 °C (fan 75 °C) and continue to bake until instant-read thermometer inserted into center of cheesecake registers about 65 °C, about 1 1/2 hours. Transfer cake to wire rack and cool 5 minutes; run paring knife between cake and side of springform pan. Cool until barely warm, 2 1/2 to 3 hours. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate until cold, at least 3 hours. (Cake can be refrigerated up to 4 days.)

5. To unmold cheesecake, remove sides of pan. Slide thin metal spatula between crust and pan bottom to loosen, then slide cake onto serving plate. Let cheesecake stand at room temperature about 30 minutes, then cut into wedges and serve.

1. Korpus: rošt v rúre posunieme do dolnej strednej polohy a rúru rozohrejeme na 165 °C (teplovzdušnú na 145 °C). V strednej mise zmiešame strúhanku z grahamových sušienok s cukrom; pridáme 5 PL (70 g) rozpusteného masla a vidličkou premiešame, kým sa strúhanka rovnomerne nenavlhčí. Dno a steny tortovej formy s odnímateľným okrajom s priemerom 23 cm potrieme väčšinou zvyšného rozpusteného masla; necháme si dosť na potretie formy v kroku 4.
2. Strúhanku vysypeme do formy a rovnomerne ju natlačíme na dno. Pečieme, kým nezavonia a po okrajoch nezačne hnednúť, asi 13 minút. Kým pripravíme plnku, necháme chladnúť na mriežke.

3. Plnka: teplotu v rúre zvýšime na 260 °C (teplovzdušnú na 240 °C). V kuchynskom robote s plochým miešadlom šľaháme krémový syr na stredne nízkej rýchlosti, aby sa rozdrobil a trochu zmäkol, asi 1 minútu. Miešadlo, dno aj steny misy dobre zotrieme gumenou stierkou; pridáme soľ a asi polovicu cukru a šľaháme na stredne nízkej rýchlosti, kým sa nespoja, asi 1 minútu. Zotrieme misu; zašľaháme zvyšný cukor, kým sa nespojí, asi 1 minútu. Zotrieme misu; pridáme kyslú smotanu, citrónovú šťavu a vanilku a šľaháme na nízkej rýchlosti, kým sa nespoja, asi 1 minútu. Zotrieme misu; pridáme žĺtky a šľaháme na stredne nízkej rýchlosti, kým sa dôkladne nespoja, asi 1 minútu. Zotrieme misu; pridávame celé vajcia po dvoch a šľaháme, kým sa dôkladne nespoja, asi 1 minútu; medzi pridávaním zotierame misu.

4. Steny formy potrieme zvyšným rozpusteným maslom. Formu postavíme na plech s okrajom (zachytí prípadné vytečenie). Plnku nalejeme na vychladnutý korpus a pečieme 10 minút; bez otvárania dvierok znížime teplotu na 95 °C (teplovzdušnú na 75 °C) a pečieme ďalej, kým vpichový teplomer v strede cheesecaku neukáže asi 65 °C, asi 1 1/2 hodiny. Koláč preložíme na mriežku a necháme 5 minút chladnúť; medzi koláč a okraj formy prejdeme nožíkom. Necháme vychladnúť, kým nie je len sotva vlažný, 2 1/2 až 3 hodiny. Pevne zabalíme do fólie a necháme v chladničke vychladiť, aspoň 3 hodiny. (V chladničke vydrží až 4 dni.)

5. Pri vyberaní z formy odstránime okraj formy. Medzi korpus a dno formy zasunieme tenkú kovovú stierku, aby sa uvoľnil, a koláč zosunieme na servírovací tanier. Cheesecake necháme asi 30 minút postáť pri izbovej teplote, potom nakrájame na trojuholníky a podávame.

cat.en: Let the cheesecake cool slowly in the turned-off oven with the door ajar; sudden temperature changes cause cracks.
cat.sk: Cheesecake nechajte pomaly chladnúť vo vypnutej rúre s pootvorenými dvierkami; prudká zmena teploty spôsobuje praskliny.

src: King Arthur Baking, "Basque Cheesecake (Tarta de Queso)"

en.v: Store leftover Basque cheesecake in the refrigerator for up to a week.

sk.v: Zvyšný baskický cheesecake uchovávame v chladničke až týždeň.

en.t: three packages (681 g) cream cheese
297 g granulated sugar
1/2 tsp (3 g) table salt
5 large eggs (≈250 g without shell)
170 g heavy cream
1. Position a rack in the center of the oven and preheat the oven to 260 °C (fan 240 °C).
2. To prepare the pan: Take two sheets of 42 cm x 31 cm parchment and crumple each into a ball. If you don’t have parchment that size, you’ll need enough to cover roughly a 38 cm square.

3. Uncrumple the parchment completely and overlap the two sheets in a cross, pressing them into a 23 cm springform pan to completely cover the bottom and sides of the pan. The paper won’t lie flush with the sides but crumpling it first will make fitting it into the pan easier.
4. Fold the overhanging parchment down over the outside edge of the pan to ensure that the top of the cake remains visible and open to the oven’s heat.
5. To make the Basque cheesecake: Place all the ingredients in the bowl of a food processor fitted with the blade attachment (2600 ml capacity is best).
6. Process the batter until it’s smooth and lump-free, about 5 minutes, scraping the bowl about halfway through.
7. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and transfer the pan to the middle rack in the oven.

8. To bake: Bake the Basque cheesecake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the top is a deep-dark brown, the edges are just set, and the center is still quite jiggly. A digital thermometer inserted 2.5 cm from the edge and 2.5 cm deep should read as close to 85 °C as possible. For best results, start checking your cheesecake at the 25-minute mark, and continue to check at 1-minute intervals until the desired doneness is reached. Taking this cheesecake out of the oven at just the right point is critical to its success.

9. Remove the cheesecake from the oven and place it on a rack; cool the cake in the pan to room temperature before slicing. Unmold and serve the cheesecake at room temperature or refrigerate and serve chilled.
10. Storage information: Store leftover Basque cheesecake in the refrigerator for up to a week.

1. Rošt dáme do stredu rúry a rúru predhrejeme na 260 °C (teplovzdušnú na 240 °C).
2. Príprava formy: dva hárky papiera na pečenie 42 × 31 cm pokrčíme do gule. Ak nemáme papier tejto veľkosti, potrebujeme toľko, aby pokryl štvorec asi 38 cm.

3. Papier úplne rozrovnáme a oba hárky prekrížime cez seba a vtlačíme do tortovej formy s odnímateľným okrajom s priemerom 23 cm tak, aby úplne pokrývali dno aj steny. Papier nebude k stenám priliehať, ale vďaka pokrčeniu sa do formy ľahšie vloží.
4. Prečnievajúci papier preložíme cez vonkajší okraj formy, aby vrch koláča zostal odkrytý a vystavený teplu rúry.
5. Baskický cheesecake: všetky suroviny dáme do kuchynského robota s nožom (najlepší je s objemom 2600 ml).
6. Cesto mixujeme dohladka a bez hrudiek, asi 5 minút; asi v polovici zotrieme steny nádoby.
7. Cesto nalejeme do pripravenej formy a formu vložíme na stredný rošt v rúre.

8. Pečenie: baskický cheesecake pečieme 25 až 30 minút, kým nie je vrch sýto tmavohnedý, okraje práve stuhnuté a stred sa ešte výrazne chveje. Digitálny teplomer zapichnutý 2,5 cm od okraja do hĺbky 2,5 cm by mal ukázať čo najbližšie k 85 °C. Najlepšie je začať kontrolovať po 25 minútach a potom kontrolovať každú 1 minútu, kým nedosiahneme požadovaný stav. Vybrať cheesecake z rúry v správnej chvíli je pre úspech rozhodujúce.

9. Cheesecake vyberieme z rúry a postavíme na mriežku; pred krájaním ho necháme vo forme vychladnúť na izbovú teplotu. Vyberieme z formy a podávame izbovej teploty, alebo ho dáme do chladničky a podávame vychladený.
10. Skladovanie: zvyšky baskického cheesecaku uchovávame v chladničke najviac týždeň.

en.v: 20 × 7.5 cm round springform pan, roasting pan, mixer, wire rack

sk.v: Okrúhla tortová forma s odnímateľným okrajom 20 × 7,5 cm, pekáč, mixér, mriežka

c.t: Use a springform pan with sides at least 7.5 cm tall, or a 23 cm pan (flatter cake), or line the sides with a paper collar. Medium peaks gently flop over when the whisk is lifted. Keep the water bath below the foil, or water seeps in and the base goes soggy.

Použite rozkladaciu formu s okrajom vysokým aspoň 7,5 cm, alebo formu s priemerom 23 cm (koláč bude plochejší), alebo okraj obložte golierom z papiera. Stredne tuhý sneh sa po zdvihnutí metličky zľahka prehne. Vodný kúpeľ držte pod alobalom, inak voda presiakne a spodok zvlhne.

en.t: 1 (225 g) package cream cheese, softened
4 tbsp (57 g) unsalted butter, softened
99 g granulated sugar, divided
Pinch of kosher salt
5 large eggs (≈250 g without shell), separated
1 packed tsp zest and 2 tbsp (30 ml) fresh juice from 1 lemon
115 g sour cream, at room temperature
38 g cake flour
2 tbsp (14 g) cornstarch
1/4 tsp (1.2 ml) cream of tartar

1. Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and preheat to 170 °C (fan 150 °C). Grease the bottom and sides of a 20 × 7.5 cm springform pan and wrap the bottom half of the pan with foil to create a waterproof seal. Set into a roasting pan.

2. In a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment, beat cream cheese, butter, 2 tbsp (30 ml) sugar, and salt on medium speed until very creamy, scraping down sides as necessary with a rubber spatula (about 2 minutes). Beat in egg yolks and lemon zest until smooth, about 30 seconds. Replace paddle attachment with whisk attachment. Whisk in the lemon juice and sour cream on medium speed, scraping down sides as necessary with a rubber spatula, until combined.

3. Sift the flour and cornstarch over the batter and whisk until completely combined. Transfer mixture to a large bowl, using a rubber spatula. Thoroughly wash and dry stand mixer bowl and whisk (a dirty bowl will prevent whites from aerating properly).
4. Using the mixer's whisk attachment, beat egg whites and cream of tartar on high speed until frothy. Slowly pour in the remaining sugar and continue to whip to medium-peak stage. Don't over-whip.
5. Fold a third of the meringue into the batter with a rubber spatula until almost combined. Gently fold in the remaining meringue in two more batches.
6. Pour the batter into the springform pan and set on the oven rack. Pour about 5 cm hot water into the roasting pan. Bake until the cake is golden and just firm in the center, 40 to 45 minutes.
7. Remove roasting pan from oven and let springform pan remain in water bath for 30 minutes. Set on wire rack to cool for another 30 minutes, then chill until set, about 3 hours. Serve.

en.t: 455 g plain or toasted sugar
4 1/2 tsp (18 g) baking powder
2 tsp (8 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt, use about half as much by volume or the same weight
225 g unsalted butter (16 tbsp), soft but cool, about 16 °C
3 large eggs (≈150 g without shell), brought to about 18 °C
15 g vanilla extract (about 1 tbsp (15 ml))
455 g whole milk, brought to about 18 °C
455 g all-purpose flour (spooned)
170 g egg whites (from 5 to 6 large eggs), for the buttercream
310 g plain or lightly toasted sugar, for the buttercream
3/4 tsp (3 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt (use half as much if iodized), for the buttercream
1/4 tsp (1 g) cream of tartar, for the buttercream
seeds from 1 split vanilla bean (optional), for the buttercream
565 g unsalted butter, softened to about 18 °C, for the buttercream
1 tsp (5 ml) vanilla extract, for the buttercream
1/4 tsp (1.25 ml) almond extract (optional), for the buttercream

1. For the Cake: Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and preheat to 180 °C (fan 160 °C). Lightly grease three 20 cm anodized aluminum cake pans and line with parchment. If you don’t have 3 pans, it’s okay to bake the cakes in stages, the batter will keep at room temperature until needed.

2. In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, combine sugar, baking powder, salt, and butter. Mix on low speed to roughly incorporate, then increase to medium and beat until fluffy and light, about 5 minutes. About halfway through, pause to scrape the bowl and beater with a flexible spatula.

3. With the mixer still running, add the eggs one at a time, letting each fully incorporate before adding the next, then dribble in the vanilla. Reduce speed to low and sprinkle in about 1/3 of the flour, then drizzle in 1/3 of the milk. Repeat with remaining flour and milk, working in thirds as before.

4. Scrape the bowl and beater with a flexible spatula, and resume mixing on medium speed for about 3 seconds to ensure everything is well combined. The batter should look creamy and thick, registering between 18 and 20 °C on a digital thermometer. (Significant deviation indicates ingredients were too warm or too cold, which can lead to textural problems with the cake.)

5. Fold batter once or twice from the bottom up with a flexible spatula, then divide evenly between prepared cake pans (about 565 g if you have a scale). Stagger pans together on the oven rack, and bake until puffed, firm, and pale gold, about 32 minutes. If your oven has very uneven heat, pause to rotate the pans after about 20 minutes. Alternatively, bake 2 layers at once and finish the third when they’re done.

6. Cool cakes directly in their pans for 1 hour, then run a butter knife around the edges to loosen. Invert onto a wire rack, peel off the parchment, and return cakes right-side-up (covered in plastic, the cakes can be left at room temperature for a few hours).

7. For the buttercream: Fill a wide pot with at least 4 cm of water and set a thick ring of crumpled foil on the bottom so the bowl will not touch the pot. Heat until steaming-hot, then adjust to a gentle simmer. Combine the egg whites, sugar, salt, cream of tartar, and vanilla seeds (if using) in the bowl of a stand mixer. Set over the steaming water, stirring and scraping constantly with a flexible spatula, until the whites hold steady at 85 °C, 10 to 12 minutes (turn up the heat if it seems slow). Transfer to the stand mixer fitted with the whisk and whip at high speed until the meringue is glossy, stiff, and cool to the touch, about 32 °C, about 10 minutes.

8. With the mixer running, add the butter 1 or 2 tbsp at a time. The meringue will lose volume and may look soupy, but it will thicken as the butter is added. The finished buttercream should be thick, creamy, and soft but not runny, about 22 °C. Mix in the vanilla and almond extract (if using) on low speed.

9. Use the buttercream right away, or seal it in a zipper-lock bag and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks or freeze for up to several months; rewarm to 22 °C and re-whip before using. If it is warmer than 23 °C it will be soft and loose: refrigerate for 15 minutes and re-whip. If it is colder than 20 °C it will be firm and dense: set it briefly over steaming water until the edges just melt, then re-whip.

10. For the Crumb Coat: Level cakes with a serrated knife and set the scraps aside for snacking. Place one layer on a heavy cast iron turntable. If you like, a waxed cardboard cake round can first be placed underneath, secured to the turntable with a scrap of damp paper towel. Top with exactly 235 ml buttercream, using an offset spatula to spread it evenly from edge to edge. Repeat with the second and third layers, then cover the sides of the cake with another 235 ml buttercream, spreading it as smoothly as you can. Refrigerate cake until the buttercream hardens, about 30 minutes.

11. To Finish: Rewhip remaining buttercream to restore its creamy consistency, then use to finish and decorate the chilled cake as desired. Let the cake sit at room temperature for at least an hour before serving, otherwise it will be too cold inside. Cut with a chef’s knife to serve, and cover the exposed edges with leftover buttercream to keep the cake moist. Under a cake dome, the cake will keep for 3 days at room temperature.

1. Cesto: rošt v rúre posunieme do dolnej strednej polohy a rúru predhrejeme na 180 °C (teplovzdušnú na 160 °C). Tri tortové formy z eloxovaného hliníka s priemerom 20 cm zľahka vymastíme a vystelieme papierom na pečenie. Ak nemáme 3 formy, môžeme piecť postupne; cesto pri izbovej teplote počká, kým ho nebudeme potrebovať.

2. V mise kuchynského robota s plochým miešadlom spojíme cukor, prášok do pečiva, soľ a maslo. Na nízkej rýchlosti zhruba premiešame, potom zvýšime na strednú a šľaháme do nadýchanej a ľahkej hmoty, asi 5 minút. Asi v polovici zastavíme a misu aj miešadlo zotrieme ohybnou stierkou.

3. Za chodu robota pridávame po jednom vajcia a každé necháme úplne zapracovať, kým pridáme ďalšie; potom prilejeme vanilku. Znížime rýchlosť na nízku a vsypeme asi 1/3 múky, potom prilejeme 1/3 mlieka. Zopakujeme so zvyšnou múkou a mliekom, opäť po tretinách.

4. Misu aj miešadlo zotrieme ohybnou stierkou a miešame na strednej rýchlosti ešte asi 3 sekundy, aby sa všetko dobre spojilo. Cesto má byť krémové a husté a digitálny teplomer v ňom má ukázať 18 až 20 °C. (Výraznejšia odchýlka znamená, že suroviny boli príliš teplé alebo príliš studené, čo môže pokaziť štruktúru koláča.)

5. Cesto ohybnou stierkou raz či dvakrát premiešame odspodu nahor a rovnomerne rozdelíme do pripravených foriem (ak máme váhu, asi 565 g). Formy rozostavíme na rošte vedľa seba a pečieme, kým nie sú nadýchané, pevné a svetlozlatisté, asi 32 minút. Ak rúra pečie veľmi nerovnomerne, asi po 20 minútach formy otočíme. Prípadne upečieme naraz 2 pláty a tretí dopečieme, keď budú hotové.

6. Pláty necháme 1 hodinu chladnúť priamo vo formách, potom po okraji prejdeme nožom na maslo, aby sa uvoľnili. Vyklopíme na mriežku, stiahneme papier a pláty obrátime späť správnou stranou nahor (prikryté fóliou môžu zostať niekoľko hodín pri izbovej teplote).

7. Krém: širší hrniec naplníme aspoň 4 cm vody a na dno položíme hrubý krúžok z pokrčeného alobalu, aby sa misa nedotýkala hrnca. Zohrejeme, kým voda nie je horúca a nepári, potom oheň upravíme na mierny var. V mise kuchynského robota spojíme bielky, cukor, soľ, vínny kameň a vanilkové semienka (ak ich používame). Postavíme nad parou a za stáleho miešania a zoškrabovania ohybnou stierkou zohrievame, kým bielky stabilne nedosiahnu 85 °C, 10 až 12 minút (ak to ide pomaly, zvýšime oheň). Misu preložíme na robot s metlou a šľaháme na vysokej rýchlosti, kým nie je snehová hmota lesklá, tuhá a na dotyk chladná, asi 32 °C, asi 10 minút.

8. Za chodu robota pridávame maslo po 1 až 2 PL. Snehová hmota stratí objem a môže vyzerať ako polievka, ale s pribúdajúcim maslom zhustne. Hotový krém má byť hustý, krémový a mäkký, no nie tekutý, asi 22 °C. Na nízkej rýchlosti vmiešame vanilku a mandľový extrakt (ak ho používame).

9. Krém použijeme hneď, alebo ho uzavrieme do uzatvárateľného vrecka a uchováme v chladničke až 2 týždne alebo v mrazničke až niekoľko mesiacov; pred použitím ho zohrejeme na 22 °C a znova vyšľaháme. Ak je teplejší ako 23 °C, bude mäkký a riedky: dáme ho na 15 minút do chladničky a znova vyšľaháme. Ak je studenší ako 20 °C, bude tuhý a hutný: krátko ho podržíme nad parou, kým sa okraje len nerozpustia, a znova vyšľaháme.

10. Základná vrstva krému: pláty zarovnáme zúbkovaným nožom (odrezky si necháme na maškrtenie). Jeden plát položíme na ťažký liatinový otočný stojan. Ak chceme, môžeme podeň najprv dať voskovanú kartónovú tortovú podložku a prichytiť ju k stojanu kúskom vlhkej papierovej utierky. Navrch dáme presne 235 ml krému a zahnutou stierkou ho rovnomerne roztrieme od okraja po okraj. Zopakujeme s druhým a tretím plátom, potom boky torty pokryjeme ďalšími 235 ml krému a roztrieme čo najhladšie. Tortu necháme v chladničke, kým krém nestuhne, asi 30 minút.

11. Dokončenie: zvyšný krém znova vyšľaháme, aby bol opäť krémový, a vychladenú tortu ním dokončíme a ozdobíme podľa chuti. Pred podávaním necháme tortu aspoň hodinu pri izbovej teplote, inak bude vnútri príliš studená. Krájame kuchárskym nožom a odkryté rezy pokryjeme zvyšným krémom, aby torta nevysychala. Pod poklopom na tortu vydrží pri izbovej teplote 3 dni.

3. Whisk wet ingredients into dry ingredients until smooth. Divide batter evenly between prepared pans and smooth cake tops with rubber spatula. Bake until cake is just firm and a toothpick inserted into center comes out with just a few moist crumbs attached, 22 to 25 minutes.
4. Let cakes cool in pans for 15 minutes. Remove cakes from pans, discard parchment, and let cool completely on wire rack, about 1 hour.

5. For the Frosting: Meanwhile, in a food processor, process butter, confectioners' sugar, cocoa, and salt until combined and smooth, about 30 seconds, scraping down sides of bowl as necessary. Add corn syrup and vanilla and process until smooth, about 30 seconds, scraping down sides of bowl as necessary. Add chocolate and process until smooth and creamy, about 30 seconds.

6. To Assemble the Cake: Place one cake, top side up, on a serving platter or cake pedestal. Using offset spatula, spread about 235 ml frosting over top of cake layer. Center second cake, bottom side up, on top, and press lightly to adhere. Spread remaining frosting evenly over top and sides of assembled cake. To decorate, use the back of a soup spoon to make decorative swirls on the cake or decorate as desired. Serve.

3. Mokré suroviny metličkou vmiešame do suchých dohladka. Cesto rovnomerne rozdelíme do pripravených foriem a povrch uhladíme gumenou stierkou. Pečieme, kým nie sú pláty práve pevné a špáradlo zapichnuté do stredu nevyjde len s niekoľkými vlhkými omrvinkami, 22 až 25 minút.

5. Poleva: medzitým v kuchynskom robote mixujeme maslo, práškový cukor, kakao a soľ, kým sa nespoja a nie sú hladké, asi 30 sekúnd; podľa potreby zotierame steny nádoby. en.t: 70 g all-purpose flour
30 g cornstarch
4 large eggs (200 g)
100 g caster or superfine sugar
1/4 tsp (0.8 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt, use half as much by volume or the same weight
3 1/2 tbsp (45 g) unsalted butter, melted, cooled slightly, and transferred to a small bowl
1. Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 177 °C (fan 157 °C). Lightly grease a 20 cm anodized aluminum cake pan and line with parchment paper.

2. In a medium bowl, whisk together flour and cornstarch until thoroughly combined. Set a fine-mesh strainer over a medium bowl and sift flour mixture. Repeat to make sure there are no lumps and set aside.

3. In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment, whisk eggs and sugar on high speed until mixture is a pale creamy color and has tripled in volume with lots of visible bubbles, about 3 minutes. Reduce speed to medium and continue whisking until mixture is smoother and more velvety in texture (some of the larger bubbles will have disappeared), about 5 minutes. Reduce speed to low and whisk until an extremely silky, smooth, and pourable stable foam forms, about 10 minutes.

4. Pour egg-sugar foam into a large, extra-wide bowl and, using a fine-mesh strainer, sift one-third of the flour mixture on top and add salt. Using a large flat spatula or spoon, fold in the flour mixture using a capital D motion: slice the spatula down through the middle, then guide the spatula back to the top following the perimeter of the bowl. Use your other hand to rotate the bowl a quarter-turn between folds. Continue folding until only a few bits of flour remain, then repeat with the remaining flour mixture, one-third at a time.

5. Add 2 to 3 tbsp (28–42 g) of the egg-flour mixture to the bowl with butter and whisk until mixture is homogeneous and emulsified, about 10 seconds; this is your liaison batter. Add half of the liaison batter to the egg-flour mixture and fold in, using motion described above, until thoroughly combined. Repeat with remaining liaison batter.
6. Scrape batter into prepared pan, then lift pan about 20 cm above work surface and drop to break any large bubbles in the batter.

7. Bake until cake is puffed, golden, and pulling away from the sides slightly and a cake tester inserted in the center comes out clean, 25 to 30 minutes (the cake will also bounce slightly when tapped with a finger). Do not open the oven before 20 minutes, or you risk the cake collapsing. Once removed from the oven, lift pan about 20 cm above work surface and drop pan; this helps prevent the cake from shrinking.

8. Invert cake onto a wire rack and let cool completely in pan, about 1 hour. Once cool, run a butter knife around the sides of the cake to loosen, remove pan and parchment paper, and place cake right side up. Serve as desired.

1. Rošt v rúre posunieme do stredu a rúru predhrejeme na 177 °C (teplovzdušnú na 157 °C). Tortovú formu z eloxovaného hliníka s priemerom 20 cm zľahka vymastíme a vystelieme papierom na pečenie.
2. V strednej mise metličkou dôkladne zmiešame múku s kukuričným škrobom. Nad strednú misu postavíme jemné sitko a múčnu zmes preosejeme. Zopakujeme, aby nezostali žiadne hrudky, a odložíme.

3. V mise kuchynského robota s metlou šľaháme vajcia s cukrom na vysokej rýchlosti, kým zmes nie je bledá a krémová, nemá trojnásobný objem a nie je v nej veľa viditeľných bubliniek, asi 3 minúty. Znížime na strednú rýchlosť a šľaháme ďalej, kým zmes nie je hladšia a zamatovejšia (niektoré väčšie bubliny zmiznú), asi 5 minút. Znížime na nízku rýchlosť a šľaháme, kým nevznikne mimoriadne hodvábna, hladká a tekutá stabilná pena, asi 10 minút.

4. Vaječnú penu prelejeme do veľkej, extra širokej misy, cez jemné sitko na ňu preosejeme tretinu múčnej zmesi a pridáme soľ. Veľkou plochou stierkou alebo lyžicou múčnu zmes vmiešavame pohybom v tvare veľkého písmena D: stierkou prerežeme zmes stredom nadol a potom ju vedieme späť hore po obvode misy. Druhou rukou medzi jednotlivými pohybmi otáčame misu o štvrť otáčky. Vmiešavame, kým nezostane len trochu múky, potom zopakujeme so zvyšnou múčnou zmesou po tretinách.

5. Do misy s maslom pridáme 2 až 3 PL (28–42 g) vaječno-múčnej zmesi a metličkou ju vymiešame, kým zmes nie je jednoliata a emulgovaná, asi 10 sekúnd; to je naše spojovacie cesto. Polovicu spojovacieho cesta pridáme do vaječno-múčnej zmesi a vmiešame opísaným pohybom, kým sa dôkladne nespojí. Zopakujeme so zvyšným spojovacím cestom.
6. Cesto zotrieme do pripravenej formy, formu zdvihneme asi 20 cm nad pracovnú dosku a pustíme ju, aby sa rozbili veľké bubliny v ceste.

7. Pečieme, kým nie je korpus nadýchaný, zlatistý, mierne sa neodťahuje od stien a skúšobná ihla zapichnutá do stredu nevyjde čistá, 25 až 30 minút (korpus pri poklepaní prstom aj mierne pruží). Rúru neotvárame skôr ako po 20 minútach, inak hrozí, že korpus spľasne. Po vybratí z rúry formu zdvihneme asi 20 cm nad pracovnú dosku a pustíme ju; pomôže to, aby sa korpus nezmršťoval.

8. Korpus vyklopíme na mriežku a necháme ho úplne vychladnúť vo forme, asi 1 hodinu. Po vychladnutí prejdeme nožom na maslo po bokoch, aby sa uvoľnil, odstránime formu aj papier a korpus obrátime správnou stranou nahor. Podávame podľa chuti.

sk.v: Zvyšný koláč uchovávame dobre zabalený pri izbovej teplote niekoľko dní; na dlhšie skladovanie ho zmrazíme.

en.t: 7 large eggs (≈350 g without shell), separated, at room temperature*
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) cream of tartar
298 g granulated sugar, divided
240 g King Arthur Unbleached All-Purpose Flour
2 1/2 tsp (10 g) baking powder
3/4 tsp (4.5 g) table salt
99 g vegetable oil
2 tsp (10 ml) King Arthur Pure Vanilla Extract
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) almond extract, or other flavor of your choice
170 g milk, at room temperature
340 g heavy cream
57 g sour cream
2 tbsp (25 g) granulated sugar
2 tsp (10 ml) King Arthur Pure Vanilla Extract or vanilla bean paste
1. To make the cake: Preheat the oven to 165 °C (fan 145 °C) with a rack in the bottom third. Have on hand an ungreased 25 cm tube or angel food cake pan.
2. In a large mixing bowl, beat the egg whites with the cream of tartar until foamy. Gradually add 99 g of the sugar and continue beating until stiff and glossy. Set aside.
3. In a medium bowl, whisk together the remaining 198 g sugar with the flour, baking powder, and salt.

4. In a large mixing bowl or bowl of your stand mixer, use the whisk attachment to beat the oil, reserved egg yolks, and extracts until pale yellow. Add the dry ingredients in thirds, alternating with the milk, beating at medium speed for 2 to 4 minutes.
5. Gently fold in the whipped egg whites with a whisk or spatula just until the batter is uniform. Scrape the bottom of the bowl to ensure the batter is evenly mixed.
6. Pour the batter into the prepared pan. Bake for 50 minutes without opening the oven; the cake will rise high above the pan then settle back almost even as it continues to bake.

7. Increase the oven temperature to 175 °C (fan 155 °C) and bake for 10 minutes more, until a gentle touch on the center of the cake leaves no indent; if you listen carefully, the cake should make a crackling sound.

8. Remove from the oven and invert the tube pan over the neck of a clean glass bottle for 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, use a thin-bladed flexible spatula to free the cake from the sides and tube of the pan. Turn the cake out onto a serving plate to finish cooling completely.
9. To make the Chantilly cream: Place all the ingredients in a large, chilled mixing bowl. Beat until the mixture holds soft peaks.
10. To serve: Sift confectioners' sugar over the cake, then slice. Top each slice with a spoonful of Chantilly cream or whipped cream; garnish with berries, if desired.
11. Storage information: Store leftover cake, well wrapped, at room temperature for several days; freeze for longer storage.

c.t: 1. To make the cake: Preheat the oven to 165 °C (fan 145 °C) with a rack in the bottom third. Have on hand an ungreased 25 cm tube or angel food cake pan.
2. In a large mixing bowl, beat the egg whites with the cream of tartar until foamy. Gradually add 74 g of the sugar and continue beating until stiff and glossy. Set aside.
3. In a medium bowl, whisk together the remaining 150 g sugar with the flour, baking powder, and salt.

4. In a large mixing bowl or bowl of your stand mixer, use the whisk attachment to beat the oil, reserved egg yolks, and extracts until pale yellow. Add the dry ingredients in thirds, alternating with the milk, beating at medium speed for 2 to 4 minutes.
5. Gently fold in the whipped egg whites with a whisk or spatula just until the batter is uniform. Scrape the bottom of the bowl to ensure the batter is evenly mixed.
6. Pour the batter into the prepared pan. Bake for 50 minutes without opening the oven; the cake will rise high above the pan then settle back almost even as it continues to bake.

7. Increase the oven temperature to 175 °C (fan 155 °C) and bake for 10 minutes more, until a gentle touch on the center of the cake leaves no indent; if you listen carefully, the cake should make a crackling sound.

8. Remove from the oven and invert the tube pan over the neck of a clean glass bottle for 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, use a thin-bladed flexible spatula to free the cake from the sides and tube of the pan. Turn the cake out onto a serving plate to finish cooling completely.
9. To make the Chantilly cream: Place all the ingredients in a large, chilled mixing bowl. Beat until the mixture holds soft peaks.
10. To serve: Sift confectioners' sugar over the cake, then slice. Top each slice with a spoonful of Chantilly cream or whipped cream; garnish with berries, if desired.
11. Storage information: Store leftover cake, well wrapped, at room temperature for several days; freeze for longer storage.
1. Cesto: rúru predhrejeme na 165 °C (teplovzdušnú na 145 °C) s roštom v dolnej tretine. Pripravíme si nevymastenú formu s komínom s priemerom 25 cm alebo formu na angel food cake.
2. Vo veľkej mise vyšľaháme bielky s vínnym kameňom do peny. Postupne pridávame 74 g cukru a šľaháme ďalej do tuhého a lesklého snehu. Odložíme.
3. V strednej mise metličkou zmiešame zvyšných 150 g cukru s múkou, práškom do pečiva a soľou.

4. Vo veľkej mise alebo mise kuchynského robota šľaháme metlou olej, odložené žĺtky a extrakty, kým zmes nie je svetložltá. Suché suroviny pridávame po tretinách striedavo s mliekom a šľaháme na strednej rýchlosti 2 až 4 minúty.
5. Metličkou alebo stierkou jemne vmiešame vyšľahaný sneh, len kým nie je cesto jednoliate. Zotrieme dno misy, aby bolo cesto rovnomerne premiešané.
6. Cesto nalejeme do pripravenej formy. Pečieme 50 minút bez otvárania rúry; koláč vystúpi vysoko nad formu a počas ďalšieho pečenia klesne takmer na úroveň okraja.
7. Teplotu v rúre zvýšime na 175 °C (teplovzdušnú na 155 °C) a pečieme ešte 10 minút, kým jemný dotyk v strede koláča nezanechá žiadnu jamku; keď dobre počúvame, koláč by mal jemne praskať.

8. Vyberieme z rúry a formu s komínom obrátime a nasadíme na hrdlo čistej sklenenej fľaše na 30 minút. Po 30 minútach tenkou ohybnou stierkou uvoľníme koláč od stien aj komína formy. Koláč vyklopíme na servírovací tanier a necháme úplne vychladnúť.
9. Krém Chantilly: všetky suroviny dáme do veľkej vychladenej misy. Šľaháme, kým zmes nedrží mäkké špičky.
10. Podávanie: koláč poprášime preosiatym práškovým cukrom a nakrájame. Na každý kúsok dáme lyžicu krému Chantilly alebo šľahačky; podľa chuti ozdobíme bobuľovým ovocím.
11. Skladovanie: zvyšky koláča dobre zabalené uchovávame pri izbovej teplote niekoľko dní; na dlhšie skladovanie ich zamrazíme.

cat.en: Separate the eggs carefully: even a little yolk in the whites stops them whipping properly.
cat.sk: Vajcia oddeľujte opatrne: aj trocha žĺtka v bielkoch zabráni ich poriadnemu vyšľahaniu.

tip.en: Zest only the bright orange peel, not the white pith underneath, which is bitter.
tip.sk: Strúhajte len sýtooranžovú časť kôry, nie bielu vrstvu pod ňou, ktorá je horká.

tip.en: Rub the lemon zest into the sugar with your fingers before mixing; it releases the oils and gives a stronger lemon flavour.
tip.sk: Citrónovú kôru pred miešaním votrite prstami do cukru; uvoľnia sa z nej oleje a chuť citróna bude výraznejšia.

tip.en: If you can't find fresh or frozen pandan leaves, simply use more pandan extract.
tip.sk: Ak nezoženiete čerstvé ani mrazené listy pandanu, jednoducho použite viac pandanového extraktu.

tip.en: Use pure matcha that isn't blended with sugar or milk powder, and sift it with the flour and baking powder for the smoothest batter.
tip.sk: Použite čistú matchu bez prímesi cukru či sušeného mlieka a preosejte ju spolu s múkou a kypriacim práškom, cesto bude čo najhladšie.

en.t: 140 g bleached cake flour
425 g cold egg whites from 12 large eggs
425 g granulated sugar
1 tbsp (15 ml) vanilla extract
25 g freshly squeezed lemon juice (2 tbsp (30 ml)) from 1 small lemon
1/4 tsp (1 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt, use half as much by volume or use the same weight
945 ml assorted fruit, such as blueberries, blackberries, and figs (optional)
25 g Fresh Lemon Syrup (2 tbsp (30 ml)), optional
170 g Lemon Chantilly, optional

1. Adjust oven rack to the middle position and preheat to 180 °C (fan 160 °C). Sift cake flour and set aside. Combine egg whites, sugar, and vanilla extract in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment. Mix on low to loosen, about 1 minute, then increase to medium-low (4 on a KitchenAid) and whip 3 minutes; the whites will be dense and dark.

2. With the mixer still running, add lemon juice and salt. Immediately increase to medium (6 on a KitchenAid) and whip 3 minutes more; the meringue will be thin but foamy. Increase to medium-high (8 on a KitchenAid) and continue whipping until the meringue is glossy white and thick enough that you can see the pattern left by the wire whisk. This can take between 2 and 4 minutes, depending on the freshness of the whites and the horsepower of your mixer. When meringue is ready, it should be soft enough to run off the wires when the whisk attachment is removed, but thick enough to mound up on itself like soft-serve in the bowl.

3. Sprinkle cake flour on top and stir with a flexible spatula to roughly combine. Switch to a folding motion, scraping from the bottom up and folding through the center, until no pockets of flour remain. Scrape the batter into a 25 cm aluminum tube pan with removable bottom (do not butter or grease pan); if you notice any small pockets of unincorporated flour, simply pause to mix them in. Bake until the cake is puffed, golden blond, and firm to the touch, about 45 minutes, or to an internal temperature of 97 °C.

4. Invert pan onto its stilts or onto a trio of cans and cool upside down until absolutely no trace of warmth remains, at least 2 hours. Slide an offset spatula around the sides of cake to loosen, remove the insert, and slide spatula under the bottom as well. Flip onto a serving plate, pulling gently on the sides of the cake to release it from the center tube. To serve, cut with a chef's knife, using a gentle sawing motion and only the slightest downward pressure. If you like, garnish with figs and berries tossed in fresh lemon syrup and finish with lemon chantilly. Wrapped tightly in plastic, leftovers will keep up to 1 week at room temperature.

1. Rošt v rúre posunieme do stredu a rúru predhrejeme na 180 °C (teplovzdušnú na 160 °C). Hladkú múku na pečivo preosejeme a odložíme. V mise kuchynského robota s metlou spojíme bielky, cukor a vanilkový extrakt. Na nízkej rýchlosti premiešame, aby sa bielky uvoľnili, asi 1 minútu, potom zvýšime na stredne nízku (4 na KitchenAide) a šľaháme 3 minúty; bielky budú husté a tmavé.

2. Za chodu robota pridáme citrónovú šťavu a soľ. Hneď zvýšime na strednú rýchlosť (6 na KitchenAide) a šľaháme ešte 3 minúty; snehová hmota bude riedka, ale penivá. Zvýšime na stredne vysokú rýchlosť (8 na KitchenAide) a šľaháme, kým nie je sneh lesklý, biely a dosť hustý, aby bolo vidno stopu po metle. Môže to trvať 2 až 4 minúty podľa čerstvosti bielkov a výkonu robota. Hotový sneh má byť dosť mäkký, aby po vybratí metly stekal z drôtov, ale dosť hustý, aby sa v mise vŕšil ako točená zmrzlina.

3. Navrch posypeme múku a ohybnou stierkou zhruba premiešame. Potom prejdeme na vmiešavanie: zoškrabujeme odspodu nahor a prekladáme cez stred, kým nezostanú žiadne múčne hniezda. Cesto zotrieme do hliníkovej formy s komínom a vyberateľným dnom s priemerom 25 cm (formu nemastíme); ak si všimneme malé hniezda nezapracovanej múky, jednoducho ich vmiešame. Pečieme, kým nie je koláč nadýchaný, zlatoplavý a na dotyk pevný, asi 45 minút, alebo kým teplota vnútri nedosiahne 97 °C.

4. Formu obrátime na jej nožičky alebo na tri plechovky a necháme chladnúť dnom nahor, kým z nej úplne nevyprchá teplo, aspoň 2 hodiny. Zahnutou stierkou prejdeme po bokoch koláča, aby sa uvoľnil, vyberieme vložku a stierku zasunieme aj pod dno. Obrátime na servírovací tanier a jemným ťahaním za boky koláč uvoľníme z komína. Krájame kuchárskym nožom jemným pílivým pohybom a len s minimálnym tlakom nadol. Ak chceme, ozdobíme figami a bobuľovým ovocím premiešaným s čerstvým citrónovým sirupom a dokončíme citrónovým krémom Chantilly. Pevne zabalené vo fólii vydržia zvyšky pri izbovej teplote až 1 týždeň.

en.t: 198 g bleached cake flour, plus extra for flouring pan
1 1/2 tsp (6 g) baking powder
4 large eggs (≈200 g without shell), room temperature
2 tsp (10 ml) vanilla extract
16 tbsp (225 g) unsalted butter, softened plus extra for greasing pan
1 tsp (3 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt use half as much by volume
248 g sugar
60 ml whole milk, room temperature
1. Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 160 °C (fan 140 °C). Generously butter a 23 × 13 cm (or 22 × 11 cm) loaf pan; dust pan liberally with flour and knock out excess flour.
2. In a medium bowl, whisk flour and baking powder to combine; set aside. In a 475 ml liquid measuring cup or medium bowl, whisk eggs and vanilla until combined; set aside.

3. In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, beat butter and salt on medium-high speed until shiny, smooth, and creamy, 2 to 3 minutes, scraping down bowl as needed. Reduce speed to medium and gradually pour in sugar (this should take about 60 seconds). Once all sugar is added, increase speed to medium-high and beat until mixture is fluffy and almost white in color, 5 to 8 minutes, scraping down bowl as needed.

4. Reduce speed to medium and gradually add egg mixture in slow, steady stream (this should take 60 to 90 seconds). Scrape down bowl. Increase speed to medium-high and beat mixture until light and fluffy, 3 to 4 minutes (mixture may look slightly broken).

5. Stop mixer and scrape down bowl. On low speed, add 1/3 of the flour mixture, beat until just combined, then add milk and beat until combined. Add another 1/3 of the flour mixture, beat until just combined, then repeat with remaining flour. Scrape bottom of bowl to ensure that batter is homogenous.

6. Transfer batter to prepared loaf pan and smooth surface with rubber spatula. Bake until golden brown and wooden skewer inserted in center of cake comes out clean, 1 hour 10 minutes to 1 hour 20 minutes. Let cake cool in pan on wire rack for 15 minutes. Invert cake onto wire rack, then turn cake right side up. Let cake sit on wire rack until mostly cool, at least 1 hour. Slice and serve.

3. V mise kuchynského robota s plochým miešadlom šľaháme maslo so soľou na stredne vysokej rýchlosti, kým nie je lesklé, hladké a krémové, 2 až 3 minúty; podľa potreby zotierame misu. Znížime na strednú rýchlosť a postupne prisypávame cukor (malo by to trvať asi 60 sekúnd). Keď je všetok cukor pridaný, zvýšime na stredne vysokú rýchlosť a šľaháme, kým nie je zmes nadýchaná a takmer biela, 5 až 8 minút; podľa potreby zotierame misu.

4. Znížime na strednú rýchlosť a postupne pomalým rovnomerným prúdom prilievame vaječnú zmes (malo by to trvať 60 až 90 sekúnd). Zotrieme misu. Zvýšime na stredne vysokú rýchlosť a šľaháme do ľahkej a nadýchanej hmoty, 3 až 4 minúty (zmes môže vyzerať mierne zrazená).

5. Robot zastavíme a zotrieme misu. Na nízkej rýchlosti pridáme 1/3 múčnej zmesi a šľaháme, len kým sa nespojí, potom pridáme mlieko a šľaháme, kým sa nespojí. Pridáme ďalšiu 1/3 múčnej zmesi, šľaháme, len kým sa nespojí, potom zopakujeme so zvyšnou múkou. Zotrieme dno misy, aby bolo cesto jednoliate.

6. Cesto preložíme do pripravenej formy a povrch uhladíme gumenou stierkou. Pečieme, kým nie je zlatohnedý a drevená špajdľa zapichnutá do stredu nevyjde čistá, 1 hodinu 10 minút až 1 hodinu 20 minút. Koláč necháme 15 minút chladnúť vo forme na mriežke. Vyklopíme ho na mriežku a obrátime správnou stranou nahor. Necháme na mriežke, kým takmer nevychladne, aspoň 1 hodinu. Nakrájame a podávame.

en.t: 24 tbsp (340 g) unsalted butter, at room temperature, at least 20 °C
298 g granulated sugar
6 large eggs (≈300 g without shell), at room temperature
2 1/4 tsp (9 g) baking powder
1 1/2 tsp (9 g) table salt
360 g King Arthur Unbleached All-Purpose Flour
1 tbsp (14 g) King Arthur Pure Vanilla Extract or vanilla bean paste
1/4 tsp (1.2 ml) almond extract, optional
170 g milk, at room temperature
67 g granulated sugar
5 tsp (25 ml) water
1/8 tsp (0.8 g) table salt
2 tsp (10 ml) King Arthur Pure Vanilla Extract
1. Preheat the oven to 175 °C (fan 155 °C).
2. Place the butter and sugar in a large mixing bowl. Beat together at medium speed until the mixture lightens in color and looks fluffy. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl.
3. Add the baking powder and salt, mixing just to combine.
4. Weigh out the flour, or measure it by gently spooning it into a measuring cup, sweeping off any excess with a straight edge. Set it aside.
5. With the mixer running at medium speed, add the first three eggs to the butter/sugar mixture one at a time. Wait until each egg is absorbed into the mixture before adding the next.

6. Add 2 tbsp (15 g) of the measured flour to the bowl after the third egg, and mix until combined. Add the fourth egg, mix until absorbed, then mix in another 2 tbsp (15 g) of flour. Continue in this fashion with the fifth and sixth eggs, alternating the addition of the egg with 2 tbsp (15 g) of the flour from the recipe.
7. Add the vanilla (or vanilla bean paste) and almond extract to the milk.

8. Add one-third of the remaining flour to the batter, beating gently to combine. Gently beat in half the milk. Mix in another third of the flour, then the remaining milk. Stir in the remaining flour. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl, then beat until the batter is smooth and fluffy, about 20 to 30 seconds at medium-high speed.

9. Thoroughly grease a 2370–2840 ml Bundt pan, using non-stick vegetable oil spray or shortening (not butter; butter tends to increase sticking). Scoop the batter into the prepared pan, smoothing the top with a spatula.

10. Bake the cake for 50 to 60 minutes, until it's starting to brown, appears set on top, and a toothpick or long skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. (If you're baking in a dark-interior pan, start checking at 45 minutes.) If the cake appears to be browning too quickly, tent it with foil for the final 15 minutes of baking.

11. Remove the cake from the oven, and gently loosen its edges using a heatproof spatula. Turn the pan over onto a cooling rack. After 10 minutes, lift the pan off the cake, and allow it to cool completely.

12. While the cake is cooling in the pan, make the glaze. Combine the sugar, water, and salt. Heat briefly, just to dissolve the sugar; a microwave works fine. Stir in the vanilla. Once you've turned the cake out of the pan onto a rack to cool, gently brush it all over with the glaze.
13. Just before serving, sift a shower of confectioners' sugar over the top, if desired. A garnish of fresh berries is lovely and tasty.
14. Store leftover cake, well wrapped, at room temperature for several days. Freeze for longer storage.

1. Rúru predhrejeme na 175 °C (teplovzdušnú na 155 °C).
2. Maslo s cukrom dáme do veľkej misy. Šľaháme na strednej rýchlosti, kým zmes nezosvetlie a nie je nadýchaná. Zotrieme steny a dno misy.
3. Pridáme prášok do pečiva a soľ a premiešame, len kým sa nespoja.
4. Múku odvážime alebo odmeriame tak, že ju lyžicou jemne nasypeme do odmerky a prebytok zarovnáme rovnou hranou. Odložíme.
5. Za chodu robota na strednej rýchlosti pridávame k maslovo-cukrovej zmesi po jednom prvé tri vajcia. Každé necháme vsiaknuť do zmesi, kým pridáme ďalšie.

6. Po treťom vajci pridáme do misy 2 PL (15 g) odváženej múky a premiešame, kým sa nespojí. Pridáme štvrté vajce, premiešame, kým sa nevstrebe, potom vmiešame ďalšie 2 PL (15 g) múky. Rovnako pokračujeme s piatym a šiestym vajcom; vajcia striedame s 2 PL (15 g) múky z receptu.
7. Do mlieka pridáme vanilku (alebo vanilkovú pastu) a mandľový extrakt.

8. Do cesta pridáme tretinu zvyšnej múky a jemne zašľaháme. Jemne zašľaháme polovicu mlieka. Vmiešame ďalšiu tretinu múky a potom zvyšné mlieko. Vmiešame zvyšnú múku. Zotrieme steny a dno misy a šľaháme, kým nie je cesto hladké a nadýchané, asi 20 až 30 sekúnd na stredne vysokej rýchlosti.

9. Bábovkovú formu (bundt) s objemom 2370 – 2840 ml dôkladne vymastíme nepriľnavým olejom v spreji alebo rastlinným tukom (nie maslom; pri masle sa koláč viac prilepí). Cesto naberieme do pripravenej formy a vrch uhladíme stierkou.

10. Koláč pečieme 50 až 60 minút, kým nezačne hnednúť, navrchu nevyzerá stuhnuto a špáradlo alebo dlhá špajdľa zapichnutá do stredu nevyjde čistá. (Ak pečieme vo forme s tmavým vnútrom, začneme kontrolovať po 45 minútach.) Ak sa zdá, že koláč hnedne príliš rýchlo, posledných 15 minút pečenia ho voľne prikryjeme alobalom.
11. Koláč vyberieme z rúry a žiaruvzdornou stierkou jemne uvoľníme okraje. Formu obrátime na mriežku. Po 10 minútach formu z koláča zdvihneme a necháme ho úplne vychladnúť.

12. Kým koláč chladne vo forme, pripravíme polevu. Zmiešame cukor, vodu a soľ. Krátko zohrejeme, len aby sa cukor rozpustil; poslúži aj mikrovlnná rúra. Vmiešame vanilku. Keď koláč vyklopíme z formy na mriežku, jemne ho celý potrieme polevou.
13. Tesne pred podávaním vrch podľa chuti poprášime preosiatym práškovým cukrom. Pekne a chutne ho dozdobí čerstvé bobuľové ovocie.
14. Zvyšky koláča dobre zabalené uchovávame pri izbovej teplote niekoľko dní. Na dlhšie skladovanie ich zamrazíme.

en.t: 395 g pecan pieces
910 g whole, unpeeled carrots (from one bag)
450 g unsalted butter
395 g white sugar
225 g light brown sugar (gently packed)
4 tsp (20 ml) ground cinnamon
4 tsp (20 ml) ground ginger
1 tbsp (12 g) baking powder
1 3/4 tsp (7 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt, use about half as much by volume or the same weight
1 tsp (6 g) baking soda
1 tsp (5 ml) grated nutmeg
3/4 tsp (3.5 ml) ground cloves
15 g vanilla extract (1 tbsp (15 ml))
6 large eggs (≈300 g without shell), straight from the fridge
310 g all-purpose flour, such as Gold Medal (spooned)
140 g whole wheat flour, not stone-ground
340 g milk (any fat percentage), for the buttercream
1 vanilla bean, split lengthwise, for the buttercream
225 g sugar, for the buttercream
45 g cornstarch, for the buttercream
3 large eggs, straight from the fridge, for the buttercream
1 tbsp (15 g) vanilla extract, for the buttercream
455 g full-fat cream cheese, softened to about 18 °C, for the buttercream
340 g unsalted butter, softened to about 18 °C, for the buttercream
2 tbsp (30 g) freshly squeezed lemon juice, for the buttercream
1 recipe Twisted Carrot Roses, optional

1. For the buttercream custard: In a 2800 ml stainless-steel saucier, bring the milk and vanilla bean to a simmer over medium heat. When it begins to bubble, turn off the heat, cover, and steep for 30 minutes (or refrigerate, covered, for up to 24 hours). Meanwhile, whisk the sugar and cornstarch together in a medium bowl, then whisk in the eggs.

2. Return the milk to a simmer; scrape the pulp from the vanilla bean into the milk and discard the pod. Whisk 120 ml of the hot milk into the eggs; repeat with a second and a third ladleful, then pour the warmed eggs into the pot. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thick and lumpy, about 3 minutes; once it bubbles sluggishly, keep cooking and whisking for 2 full minutes more, until smooth.

3. Off the heat, stir in the vanilla extract, then pour the custard into a large baking dish, press plastic wrap against the surface, and refrigerate until thick and cooled to about 20 °C, about 1 hour (or up to 1 week; let it warm back to about 20 °C before using).

4. For the buttercream: In a stand mixer fitted with the paddle, beat the cream cheese and butter on medium speed until fluffy and light, about 5 minutes. Stir the custard into a thick, dough-like mass. Scrape the bowl, switch to the whisk, and whip on medium speed, adding the custard a few tbsp at a time; then drizzle in the lemon juice and, if you like, a pinch of salt. Scrape the bowl and whip a few seconds more; the buttercream should be light and creamy but thick enough to hang from a spoon.

5. Use the buttercream right away, or seal it in a zipper-lock bag and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks or freeze for up to several months; rewarm to about 22 °C and re-whip before using. If it seems stiff or greasy, melt about 235 ml of it in the microwave (about 30 seconds) and whip it back in on medium-high for 15 seconds; if it seems loose, refrigerate the bowl for 15 minutes, then whip on medium-high for 3 minutes.

6. Getting Ready: To better synchronize the downtime in both recipes, prepare the cream cheese buttercream before the cake. Adjust oven rack to the middle position and preheat to 180 °C (fan 160 °C). Toast the pecans on a baking sheet until golden brown, about 10 minutes, and cool completely. Meanwhile, peel, trim, and shred the carrots, then measure out 680 g (1420 ml, firmly packed). This can be refrigerated up to 1 week in a zip-top bag.

7. In a 1820 ml stainless steel saucier, completely melt the butter over medium-low heat. Increase to medium and simmer, stirring with a heat-resistant spatula while the butter hisses and pops. Continue cooking and stirring, scraping up any brown bits that form along the pan, until the butter is golden-yellow and perfectly silent. Pour into a heat-safe measuring cup, along with all the toasty brown bits, and proceed as directed, or cover and refrigerate up to 1 week; melt before using.

8. For the Cake: Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and preheat to 180 °C (fan 160 °C). Lightly grease three 20 cm anodized aluminum cake pans and line with parchment. If you don’t have 3 pans, it’s okay to bake the cakes in stages; the batter will keep at room temperature until needed.

9. Combine white sugar, brown sugar, cinnamon, ginger, baking powder, salt, baking soda, nutmeg, cloves, vanilla, and eggs in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment. Mix on low to moisten, then increase to medium and whip until thick and fluffy, about 8 minutes. Meanwhile, whisk together all-purpose and whole wheat flours. Drizzle in the brown butter in a steady stream, then reduce speed to low and add the flours. Once smooth, fold in shredded carrots and pecans with a flexible spatula.

10. Divide batter between the prepared cake pans, about 935 g each. If you don't have 3 pans, the remaining batter can be held at room temperature up to 3 hours. Bake until cakes are golden, about 45 minutes. A toothpick inserted into the center will have a few crumbs still attached, and your fingertip will leave a slight indentation in the puffy crust.

11. Cool cakes directly in their pans for 1 hour, then run a butter knife around the edges to loosen. Invert onto a wire rack, peel off the parchment, and return cakes right side up (covered in plastic, the cakes can be left at room temperature for a few hours).

12. For the Crumb Coat: Level cakes with a serrated knife and set the scraps aside for snacking. Place one layer on a heavy cast iron turntable. If you like, a waxed cardboard cake round can first be placed underneath, secured to the turntable with a scrap of damp paper towel. Top with exactly 235 ml buttercream, using an offset spatula to spread it evenly from edge to edge. Repeat with the second and third layers, then cover the sides of the cake with another 235 ml buttercream, spreading it as smoothly as you can. Refrigerate cake until the buttercream hardens, about 30 minutes.

13. Re-whip remaining buttercream to restore its creamy consistency, then use to decorate the chilled cake as desired; finish with twisted carrot roses (optional). Let the cake return to cool room temperature before serving. Under a cake dome or an inverted pot, the frosted cake and carrot roses will keep 24 hours at cool room temperature. After cutting, wrap leftover slices individually and store at cool room temperature up to 2 days more.

c.t: 1. For the buttercream custard: In a 2800 ml stainless-steel saucier, bring the milk and vanilla bean to a simmer over medium heat. When it begins to bubble, turn off the heat, cover, and steep for 30 minutes (or refrigerate, covered, for up to 24 hours). Meanwhile, whisk the sugar and cornstarch together in a medium bowl, then whisk in the eggs.

2. Return the milk to a simmer; scrape the pulp from the vanilla bean into the milk and discard the pod. Whisk 120 ml of the hot milk into the eggs; repeat with a second and a third ladleful, then pour the warmed eggs into the pot. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thick and lumpy, about 3 minutes; once it bubbles sluggishly, keep cooking and whisking for 2 full minutes more, until smooth.

3. Off the heat, stir in the vanilla extract, then pour the custard into a large baking dish, press plastic wrap against the surface, and refrigerate until thick and cooled to about 20 °C, about 1 hour (or up to 1 week; let it warm back to about 20 °C before using).

4. For the buttercream: In a stand mixer fitted with the paddle, beat the cream cheese and butter on medium speed until fluffy and light, about 5 minutes. Stir the custard into a thick, dough-like mass. Scrape the bowl, switch to the whisk, and whip on medium speed, adding the custard a few tbsp at a time; then drizzle in the lemon juice and, if you like, a pinch of salt. Scrape the bowl and whip a few seconds more; the buttercream should be light and creamy but thick enough to hang from a spoon.

5. Use the buttercream right away, or seal it in a zipper-lock bag and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks or freeze for up to several months; rewarm to about 22 °C and re-whip before using. If it seems stiff or greasy, melt about 235 ml of it in the microwave (about 30 seconds) and whip it back in on medium-high for 15 seconds; if it seems loose, refrigerate the bowl for 15 minutes, then whip on medium-high for 3 minutes.

6. Getting Ready: To better synchronize the downtime in both recipes, prepare the cream cheese buttercream before the cake. Adjust oven rack to the middle position and preheat to 180 °C (fan 160 °C). Toast the pecans on a baking sheet until golden brown, about 10 minutes, and cool completely. Meanwhile, peel, trim, and shred the carrots, then measure out 680 g (1420 ml, firmly packed). This can be refrigerated up to 1 week in a zip-top bag.

7. In a 1820 ml stainless steel saucier, completely melt the butter over medium-low heat. Increase to medium and simmer, stirring with a heat-resistant spatula while the butter hisses and pops. Continue cooking and stirring, scraping up any brown bits that form along the pan, until the butter is golden-yellow and perfectly silent. Pour into a heat-safe measuring cup, along with all the toasty brown bits, and proceed as directed, or cover and refrigerate up to 1 week; melt before using.

8. For the Cake: Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and preheat to 180 °C (fan 160 °C). Lightly grease three 20 cm anodized aluminum cake pans and line with parchment. If you don’t have 3 pans, it’s okay to bake the cakes in stages; the batter will keep at room temperature until needed.

9. Combine white sugar, brown sugar, cinnamon, ginger, baking powder, salt, baking soda, nutmeg, cloves, vanilla, and eggs in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment. Mix on low to moisten, then increase to medium and whip until thick and fluffy, about 8 minutes. Meanwhile, whisk together all-purpose and whole wheat flours. Drizzle in the brown butter in a steady stream, then reduce speed to low and add the flours. Once smooth, fold in shredded carrots and pecans with a flexible spatula.

10. Divide batter between the prepared cake pans, about 935 g each. If you don't have 3 pans, the remaining batter can be held at room temperature up to 3 hours. Bake until cakes are golden, about 45 minutes. A toothpick inserted into the center will have a few crumbs still attached, and your fingertip will leave a slight indentation in the puffy crust.

11. Cool cakes directly in their pans for 1 hour, then run a butter knife around the edges to loosen. Invert onto a wire rack, peel off the parchment, and return cakes right side up (covered in plastic, the cakes can be left at room temperature for a few hours).

12. For the Crumb Coat: Level cakes with a serrated knife and set the scraps aside for snacking. Place one layer on a heavy cast iron turntable. If you like, a waxed cardboard cake round can first be placed underneath, secured to the turntable with a scrap of damp paper towel. Top with exactly 235 ml buttercream, using an offset spatula to spread it evenly from edge to edge. Repeat with the second and third layers, then cover the sides of the cake with another 235 ml buttercream, spreading it as smoothly as you can. Refrigerate cake until the buttercream hardens, about 30 minutes.

13. Re-whip remaining buttercream to restore its creamy consistency, then use to decorate the chilled cake as desired; finish with twisted carrot roses (optional). Let the cake return to cool room temperature before serving. Under a cake dome or an inverted pot, the frosted cake and carrot roses will keep 24 hours at cool room temperature. After cutting, wrap leftover slices individually and store at cool room temperature up to 2 days more.

1. Vanilkový krém do krému: v 2,8-litrovom nerezovom rendlíku privedieme na strednom ohni mlieko s vanilkovým strukom k miernemu varu. Keď začne bublať, oheň vypneme, prikryjeme a necháme 30 minút lúhovať (alebo prikryté v chladničke až 24 hodín). Medzitým v strednej mise metličkou zmiešame cukor s kukuričným škrobom a potom zašľaháme vajcia.

2. Mlieko znova privedieme k miernemu varu; do mlieka vyškrabeme dužinu z vanilkového struku a struk vyhodíme. Do vajec zašľaháme 120 ml horúceho mlieka; zopakujeme s druhou a treťou naberačkou, potom zohriate vajcia vlejeme do hrnca. Za stáleho šľahania varíme na strednom ohni, kým zmes nie je hustá a hrudkovitá, asi 3 minúty; keď začne lenivo bublať, varíme a šľaháme ešte celé 2 minúty, kým nie je hladká.

3. Mimo ohňa vmiešame vanilkový extrakt, krém nalejeme do veľkej zapekacej misy, na povrch pritlačíme fóliu a necháme v chladničke, kým nezhustne a nevychladne na asi 20 °C, asi 1 hodinu (alebo až 1 týždeň; pred použitím ho necháme zohriať späť na asi 20 °C).

4. Krém: v kuchynskom robote s plochým miešadlom šľaháme krémový syr s maslom na strednej rýchlosti do nadýchanej a ľahkej hmoty, asi 5 minút. Vanilkový krém premiešame na hustú hmotu podobnú cestu. Zotrieme misu, vymeníme miešadlo za metlu a šľaháme na strednej rýchlosti, pričom po niekoľkých lyžiciach pridávame vanilkový krém; potom prilejeme citrónovú šťavu a podľa chuti štipku soli. Zotrieme misu a šľaháme ešte niekoľko sekúnd; krém má byť ľahký a krémový, ale dosť hustý, aby visel z lyžice.

5. Krém použijeme hneď, alebo ho uzavrieme do uzatvárateľného vrecka a uchováme v chladničke až 2 týždne alebo v mrazničke až niekoľko mesiacov; pred použitím ho zohrejeme na asi 22 °C a znova vyšľaháme. Ak sa zdá tuhý alebo mastný, asi 235 ml z neho roztopíme v mikrovlnnej rúre (asi 30 sekúnd) a 15 sekúnd ho zašľaháme späť na stredne vysokej rýchlosti; ak sa zdá riedky, misu dáme na 15 minút do chladničky a potom šľaháme 3 minúty na stredne vysokej rýchlosti.

6. Príprava: aby sa prestávky v oboch receptoch lepšie zladili, pripravíme krém zo smotanového syra ešte pred koláčom. Rošt v rúre posunieme do stredu a rúru predhrejeme na 180 °C (teplovzdušnú na 160 °C). Pekanové orechy opražíme na plechu dozlatista, asi 10 minút, a necháme úplne vychladnúť. Medzitým mrkvu olúpeme, zarovnáme konce, nastrúhame a odmeriame 680 g (1420 ml, pevne natlačenej). V uzatvárateľnom vrecku vydrží v chladničke až 1 týždeň.

7. V 1,82-litrovom nerezovom rendlíku na stredne miernom ohni úplne roztopíme maslo. Zvýšime na stredný oheň a za miešania žiaruvzdornou stierkou varíme, kým maslo syčí a praská. Varíme a miešame ďalej a zoškrabujeme hnedé kúsky, ktoré sa tvoria na dne, kým nie je maslo zlatožlté a úplne neutíchne. Prelejeme ho aj so všetkými opraženými hnedými kúskami do žiaruvzdornej odmerky a pokračujeme podľa postupu, alebo ho prikryjeme a uchováme v chladničke až 1 týždeň; pred použitím ho roztopíme.

8. Cesto: rošt v rúre posunieme do dolnej strednej polohy a rúru predhrejeme na 180 °C (teplovzdušnú na 160 °C). Tri tortové formy z eloxovaného hliníka s priemerom 20 cm zľahka vymastíme a vystelieme papierom na pečenie. Ak nemáme 3 formy, môžeme piecť postupne; cesto pri izbovej teplote počká, kým ho nebudeme potrebovať.

9. V mise kuchynského robota s metlou spojíme biely cukor, hnedý cukor, škoricu, zázvor, prášok do pečiva, soľ, sódu bikarbónu, muškátový oriešok, klinčeky, vanilku a vajcia. Na nízkej rýchlosti premiešame, aby sa navlhčili, potom zvýšime na strednú a šľaháme do hustej a nadýchanej hmoty, asi 8 minút. Medzitým metličkou zmiešame hladkú a celozrnnú múku. Rovnomerným prúdom prilejeme hnedé maslo, potom znížime rýchlosť na nízku a pridáme múku. Keď je cesto hladké, ohybnou stierkou vmiešame nastrúhanú mrkvu a pekanové orechy.

10. Cesto rozdelíme do pripravených foriem, asi 935 g do každej. Ak nemáme 3 formy, zvyšné cesto počká pri izbovej teplote až 3 hodiny. Pečieme, kým nie sú pláty zlatisté, asi 45 minút. Na špáradle zapichnutom do stredu zostane ešte niekoľko omrviniek a končekom prsta zanecháme v nadýchanej kôrke mierny odtlačok.

11. Pláty necháme 1 hodinu chladnúť priamo vo formách, potom po okraji prejdeme nožom na maslo, aby sa uvoľnili. Vyklopíme na mriežku, stiahneme papier a pláty obrátime späť správnou stranou nahor (prikryté fóliou môžu zostať niekoľko hodín pri izbovej teplote).

12. Základná vrstva krému: pláty zarovnáme zúbkovaným nožom (odrezky si necháme na maškrtenie). Jeden plát položíme na ťažký liatinový otočný stojan. Ak chceme, môžeme podeň najprv dať voskovanú kartónovú tortovú podložku a prichytiť ju k stojanu kúskom vlhkej papierovej utierky. Navrch dáme presne 235 ml krému a zahnutou stierkou ho rovnomerne roztrieme od okraja po okraj. Zopakujeme s druhým a tretím plátom, potom boky torty pokryjeme ďalšími 235 ml krému a roztrieme čo najhladšie. Tortu necháme v chladničke, kým krém nestuhne, asi 30 minút.

13. Zvyšný krém znova vyšľaháme, aby bol opäť krémový, a vychladenú tortu ním ozdobíme podľa chuti; dokončíme stočenými mrkvovými ružičkami (nepovinné). Pred podávaním necháme tortu zohriať na chladnejšiu izbovú teplotu. Pod poklopom na tortu alebo obráteným hrncom vydrží potretá torta aj s mrkvovými ružičkami 24 hodín pri chladnejšej izbovej teplote. Po nakrojení zvyšné kúsky zabalíme jednotlivo a uchováme pri chladnejšej izbovej teplote ešte najviac 2 dni.

144 g light brown sugar (lightly packed)
1 1/2 tsp (4.5 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt, use half as much by volume
1 tbsp (15 ml) vanilla extract
1 tbsp (15 ml) red gel paste food coloring (optional)
3 large eggs (≈150 g without shell), room temperature
240 ml buttermilk, room temperature
340 g milk (any fat percentage), for the buttercream
1 vanilla bean, split lengthwise, for the buttercream
225 g sugar, for the buttercream
45 g cornstarch, for the buttercream
3 large eggs, straight from the fridge, for the buttercream
1 tbsp (15 g) vanilla extract, for the buttercream
455 g full-fat cream cheese, softened to about 18 °C, for the buttercream
340 g unsalted butter, softened to about 18 °C, for the buttercream
2 tbsp (30 g) freshly squeezed lemon juice, for the buttercream

1. For the buttercream custard: In a 2800 ml stainless-steel saucier, bring the milk and vanilla bean to a simmer over medium heat. When it begins to bubble, turn off the heat, cover, and steep for 30 minutes (or refrigerate, covered, for up to 24 hours). Meanwhile, whisk the sugar and cornstarch together in a medium bowl, then whisk in the eggs.

2. Return the milk to a simmer; scrape the pulp from the vanilla bean into the milk and discard the pod. Whisk 120 ml of the hot milk into the eggs; repeat with a second and a third ladleful, then pour the warmed eggs into the pot. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thick and lumpy, about 3 minutes; once it bubbles sluggishly, keep cooking and whisking for 2 full minutes more, until smooth.

3. Off the heat, stir in the vanilla extract, then pour the custard into a large baking dish, press plastic wrap against the surface, and refrigerate until thick and cooled to about 20 °C, about 1 hour (or up to 1 week; let it warm back to about 20 °C before using).

4. For the buttercream: In a stand mixer fitted with the paddle, beat the cream cheese and butter on medium speed until fluffy and light, about 5 minutes. Stir the custard into a thick, dough-like mass. Scrape the bowl, switch to the whisk, and whip on medium speed, adding the custard a few tbsp at a time; then drizzle in the lemon juice and, if you like, a pinch of salt. Scrape the bowl and whip a few seconds more; the buttercream should be light and creamy but thick enough to hang from a spoon.

5. Use the buttercream right away, or seal it in a zipper-lock bag and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks or freeze for up to several months; rewarm to about 22 °C and re-whip before using. If it seems stiff or greasy, melt about 235 ml of it in the microwave (about 30 seconds) and whip it back in on medium-high for 15 seconds; if it seems loose, refrigerate the bowl for 15 minutes, then whip on medium-high for 3 minutes.

6. Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 175 °C (fan 155 °C). Grease two 20 cm round cake pans with butter and cover the bottom with a round of parchment paper. Lightly dust the insides of the cake pans with cocoa powder and discard any excess by tapping the pans upside down. (For cupcakes, line a muffin pan with baking cups.)
7. In a medium bowl, sift the flour, 50 g cocoa, and baking soda together and lightly whisk to combine. Set aside.

8. In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, beat the butter, granulated sugar, brown sugar, salt, and vanilla extract on low speed to roughly incorporate; then increase speed to medium and beat until soft, fluffy, and pale, 5 to 7 minutes, using a flexible spatula to scrape as needed.

9. With the mixer running on its lowest speed, drizzle in the food coloring (if using). Gradually increase the speed to medium and mix until the coloring is evenly distributed, about 30 seconds, stopping to scrape down the sides of the bowl if needed. With the mixer on low speed, add the eggs one by one, briefly increasing the mixer speed after each addition until each egg is fully incorporated. Once fully mixed, stop mixer and use a flexible spatula to scrape down the sides of the bowl.

10. Add a third of the flour-cocoa mixture to the butter-egg mixture, then start mixer on low speed and gradually increase to medium speed, until no dry flour remains, about 30 seconds. On low speed, slowly add a third of the buttermilk and beat until fully incorporated, about 30 seconds. Scrape down the bowl as needed, and repeat adding and alternating with half of the remaining flour mixture, half of the remaining buttermilk, then finally the remaining flour mixture, and the remaining buttermilk. With a rubber spatula, scrape the paddle clean and give the batter a final stir, making sure to scrape the bottom of the bowl.

11. For Cupcakes: Line standard-size muffin pan with baking-cup liners. Distribute the batter evenly among the baking cups so each is about 3/4 full. Bake for 24 to 26 minutes, or until a tester comes out clean. Repeat with remaining batter. Let cool completely before frosting. Once cool, use an offset spatula to spread the frosting on top of each cupcake.

12. For a Layer Cake: Scrape the batter into the prepared pans and bake until a toothpick or cake tester inserted into cake center comes out clean, 25 to 30 minutes. Cool cakes in their pans on a cooling rack for 15 minutes. Run an offset spatula or butter knife around edges of cakes, then invert cake onto a plate and transfer back to the rack to cool completely, at least 1 hour.

13. To Crumb Coat the Cake: Using a serrated knife, level cakes. Place one layer on a turntable. If you like, a waxed cardboard cake round can first be placed underneath, secured to the turntable with a scrap of damp paper towel. Top with 235 ml frosting, using an offset spatula to spread it evenly from edge to edge. Top with the second layer and cover the sides of the cake with 235 ml frosting, spread into an even and smooth layer. Refrigerate cake until frosting is firm to the touch, about 30 minutes.
14. To Finish the Cake: Spread the top and sides of the cake with the remaining frosting to decorate as desired. Allow the cake to come to room temperature before serving.
